title: Using Continuity Binder
clearDataQuestion: What happens if I clear my browser data?
clearDataAnswer: Browser data can include your local binder and clearing it can permanently delete the binder. Create an encrypted backup first.
recoveryQuestion: Can Continuity Binder recover my passphrase?
recoveryAnswer: No. Your passphrase is not stored and there is no password recovery.
encryptionQuestion: What does encrypted at rest mean?
encryptionAnswer: Records are encrypted before they are written to browser storage. The vault uses AES-GCM and a passphrase-derived wrapping key.
serverQuestion: Does my information go to a server?
serverAnswer: Binder entries are processed locally. The application has no binder-data backend and makes no application network requests.
offlineAnswer: After the application has loaded once, its app shell can reopen offline on the same device.
moveComputerQuestion: How do I move to another computer?
moveComputerAnswer: Create an encrypted backup, transfer that file yourself, install or open Continuity Binder on the other device, and restore it with the same passphrase.
exportDifferenceQuestion: What is the difference between a readable export and an encrypted backup?
exportDifferenceAnswer: A readable archive and printed binder can be read without your passphrase. An encrypted backup remains encrypted and is the restorable format.
willAnswer: No. Continuity Binder is an organizational tool and does not create or replace legal instruments. Verify them with appropriate professionals.
passwordsAnswer: Record where credentials and recovery materials are kept, not plaintext passwords or secrets in a readable export.
reviewQuestion: How often should I review the binder?
reviewAnswer: Review it after major household changes and on a regular schedule that suits your family.
printAnswer: Open Binder Preview, choose the masking and inclusion options, then use Print / Save PDF.
eraseQuestion: How do I permanently erase it?
eraseAnswer: Use Erase local binder on the unlock screen, and remember that exported or printed copies must be destroyed separately.
